# A Democratic wave reshapes Congress

Democrats won control of both chambers, ending the Republican trifecta. Some vote counts were still incomplete in the latest reporting used here; estimates and projections are labeled rather than presented as certified totals.

## Chamber balance: 2024 to 2026

The 119th Congress convened with narrow Republican control. For the 120th Congress, CBS News projected a Democratic House range of 254–267 seats on Nov. 11 and later projected a 56–44 Democratic Senate after Alaska was called. The House bars show the midpoint of the reported range for visual comparison only; whiskers show its full range.

```{r}
#| label: chamber-composition
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

composition <- tribble(
  ~Congress, ~Chamber, ~Party, ~Seats, ~Low, ~High,
  "119th (2025–27)", "House", "Democratic", 215, 215, 215,
  "119th (2025–27)", "House", "Republican", 220, 220, 220,
  "119th (2025–27)", "Senate", "Democratic", 47, 47, 47,
  "119th (2025–27)", "Senate", "Republican", 53, 53, 53,
  "120th (2027–29)", "House", "Democratic", 260.5, 254, 267,
  "120th (2027–29)", "House", "Other / not Democratic", 174.5, 168, 181,
  "120th (2027–29)", "Senate", "Democratic", 56, 56, 56,
  "120th (2027–29)", "Senate", "Republican", 44, 44, 44
) |>
  mutate(
    category = paste(Chamber, Congress, sep = " · "),
    hover = paste0(
      Congress, "<br>", Chamber, " · ", Party, ": ",
      if_else(Low == High, as.character(Seats), paste0(Low, "–", High)),
      " seats",
      if_else(Low != High, "<br>Bar height uses range midpoint; whiskers show range.", "")
    )
  )

composition_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = composition,
  x = ~category,
  y = ~Seats,
  color = ~Party,
  colors = c(
    "Democratic" = "#1d4ed8",
    "Republican" = "#b91c1c",
    "Other / not Democratic" = "#64748b"
  ),
  type = "bar",
  text = ~hover,
  hoverinfo = "text",
  error_y = list(
    type = "data",
    array = composition$High - composition$Seats,
    arrayminus = composition$Seats - composition$Low,
    visible = TRUE,
    color = "#334155",
    thickness = 1.5,
    width = 5
  ),
  xaxis = "x",
  yaxis = "y"
) |>
  layout(
    barmode = "group",
    xaxis = list(title = NULL),
    yaxis = list(title = "Seats", rangemode = "tozero"),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
    margin = list(t = 30, b = 50),
    annotations = list(
      list(x = 0.5, y = 0.99, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
           text = "House / Senate series share colors; hover for each range.",
           showarrow = FALSE, font = list(size = 11, color = "#64748b"))
    )
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

composition_plot
```

::: {.source-note}
The 119th Congress composition reflects the post-2024 election starting balance (House: 215 Democrats, 220 Republicans; Senate: 47 Democratic caucus members, 53 Republicans). For 2026, the House range is CBS News' Nov. 11 estimate and the Senate balance is CBS News' Nov. 17 projection. Sources: [CBS House and Senate overview](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2026-midterm-election-results-where-democrats-won/), [CBS Alaska Senate result](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alaska-2026-senate-sullivan-peltola/). The 2026 House non-Democratic range is the mathematical remainder from 435; it is not labeled as an all-Republican count.
:::

## The president's party and House losses

The bars show House seat change for the president's party at each midterm. The 2026 result is intentionally not plotted as an exact seat swing: available reporting confirms Democratic control but gives a range, not a final certified count.

```{r}
#| label: historical-midterms
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

midterms <- tribble(
  ~year, ~president_party, ~house_change,
  1946, "Democratic", -55,
  1950, "Democratic", -28,
  1954, "Republican", -18,
  1958, "Republican", -48,
  1962, "Democratic", -4,
  1966, "Democratic", -47,
  1970, "Republican", -12,
  1974, "Republican", -48,
  1978, "Democratic", -15,
  1982, "Republican", -26,
  1986, "Republican", -5,
  1990, "Republican", -8,
  1994, "Democratic", -54,
  1998, "Democratic", 5,
  2002, "Republican", 8,
  2006, "Republican", -30,
  2010, "Democratic", -63,
  2014, "Democratic", -13,
  2018, "Republican", -41,
  2022, "Democratic", -9
) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(
    average = vapply(
      seq_along(house_change),
      \(i) if (i >= 5) mean(house_change[(i - 4):i]) else NA_real_,
      numeric(1)
    ),
    hover = paste0(year, " · ", president_party, " president",
                   "<br>President-party House change: ", house_change, " seats")
  )

historical_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = midterms,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~house_change,
  type = "bar",
  name = "House seat change",
  marker = list(color = ifelse(midterms$house_change < 0, "#b91c1c", "#1d4ed8")),
  text = ~hover,
  hoverinfo = "text"
) |>
  add_lines(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~average,
    name = "Five-midterm average",
    line = list(color = "#172554", width = 3),
    hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.1f} seats<extra>Five-midterm average</extra>"
  ) |>
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = NULL, dtick = 4, range = c(1944, 2028)),
    yaxis = list(title = "Seats gained / lost", zeroline = TRUE),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
    margin = list(t = 30, b = 50),
    annotations = list(
      list(x = 2026, y = 0, xref = "x", yref = "y",
           text = "2026: Democratic control; exact House swing pending",
           showarrow = TRUE, ax = -90, ay = -55,
           font = list(size = 11, color = "#334155"))
    )
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)

historical_plot
```

::: {.source-note}
Historical seat changes are the net change in House seats for the president's party at midterm elections, compiled from official election results. 2018 is shown as a 41-seat Republican loss, consistent with the final House net change. The 2026 annotation is not a numeric result. Source context: [Office of the Historian, U.S. House](https://history.house.gov/Institution/Party-Divisions/Party-Divisions/).
:::

## Selected 2026 results

These are projected outcomes reported by CBS News, not a substitute for state-certified canvasses. Percentages are included only where the cited source reported a dated figure; other vote totals are left out rather than inferred.

```{r}
#| label: key-races-table
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

key_races <- tribble(
  ~State, ~Office, ~Winner, ~Party, ~Opponent, ~reported_result,
  "Maine", "Senate", "Troy Jackson", "Democratic", "Susan Collins", "CBS projected win",
  "North Carolina", "Senate", "Roy Cooper", "Democratic", "Michael Whatley", "CBS projected win",
  "Michigan", "Senate", "Abdul El-Sayed", "Democratic", "Mike Rogers", "CBS projected win",
  "Ohio", "Senate", "Sherrod Brown", "Democratic", "Jon Husted", "CBS projected win",
  "Georgia", "Senate", "Jon Ossoff", "Democratic", "Republican challenger", "CBS projected hold",
  "New Hampshire", "Senate", "Chris Pappas", "Democratic", "Republican challenger", "CBS projected win",
  "Texas", "Senate", "James Talarico", "Democratic", "Ken Paxton", "CBS projected win",
  "Florida", "Senate", "Ashley Moody", "Republican", "Democratic challenger", "CBS projected hold",
  "Georgia", "Governor", "Keisha Lance Bottoms", "Democratic", "Rick Jackson", "54.3% to 45.7%; 99% counted Nov. 11",
  "Texas", "Governor", "Gina Hinojosa", "Democratic", "Greg Abbott", "CBS projected flip",
  "Pennsylvania", "Governor", "Josh Shapiro", "Democratic", "Republican challenger", "Re-elected by about 22 points"
)

DT::datatable(
  key_races,
  rownames = FALSE,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(pageLength = 8, dom = "tip", order = list(), autoWidth = TRUE),
  caption = htmltools::tags$caption(
    style = "caption-side: top; text-align: left;",
    "Selected outcomes · filter any column"
  )
)
```

The 2026 Senate result differs substantially from the earlier scenario numbers sometimes circulated online: CBS reported Democratic wins in Maine, North Carolina, Michigan, Ohio, Georgia, New Hampshire and Texas, while Republicans held Florida. See the [CBS results overview](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/2026-midterm-election-results-where-democrats-won/) and [Senate results page](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/senate-election-results-2026/). Pennsylvania's Josh Shapiro is included as a governor's race; Abigail Spanberger's Virginia victory was in 2025, not a 2026 midterm race.
